reconstructed_theorem_text: For every finite-dimensional real inner-product space E, every function V : E -> R, and every real m > 0, if V is Frechet differentiable on all of E and m-strongly convex on all of E, then there exists p in E such that V(p) <= V(x) for every x in E and the real inner-product gradient of V at p is zero.
objects: A finite-dimensional real inner-product space E; a real-valued function V on E; a real modulus m; and an existentially produced point p in E.
domains: E is an arbitrary finite-dimensional real inner-product space, V : E -> R, m : R, and p : E.
quantifiers: Universal over E, V, and m; conditional on the listed hypotheses; existential over p; the global-minimum condition is universal over every x in E.
assumptions: m > 0; V is genuinely Frechet differentiable over E; V is m-strongly convex on Set.univ (the whole space).
conclusion: There exists p in E with IsMinOn V Set.univ p, meaning V(p) <= V(x) for all x in E, and gradient V p = 0.
scopes: Whole-space existence and stationarity only. No minimizer is supplied as input. The statement does not explicitly claim uniqueness, a numerical location bound, or a transport estimate.
constant_dependencies: The strong-convexity modulus m is any positive real. There is no numerical bound or universal numerical constant in the conclusion.
